text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"San Diego","level":"city","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance (just cause eviction)","requirement":"Landlords may terminate a covered tenancy only for listed at-fault just causes (e.g., nonpayment, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, refusal of entry, unlawful use) or no-fault just causes (landlord/family occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order requiring vacancy of at least 30 days, substantial remodel or demolition). Written notice must state the cause. Curable violations require a prior notice and opportunity to cure. No-fault terminations require 30 or 60 days' written notice (per Civ. Code 1946.1) stating the basis, the right to relocation assistance, and the right of offer to renew. Landlords must pay relocation assistance by direct payment or rent waiver. Landlords must give tenants a written notice of the Ordinance and the SDHC Tenant Protection Guide. Notice to SDHC is required within 3 business days of notice to the tenant, but not until 30 days after SDHC creates its portal (not currently in effect). Landlords must make required disclosures before any buyout offer, and buyout agreements must meet formal requirements or are void. Retaliation is banned.","key_value":"Relocation assistance for no-fault termination: 2 months of actual rent, or 3 months if the tenant is a senior (62+) or disabled, paid directly or by rent waiver, regardless of income or length of tenancy; right of offer if the unit is re-offered within 5 years (not for withdrawal from the rental market).","coverage_conditions":"Applies to residential tenancies (right to occupy for more than 30 days) in dwelling units, including rented dwellings in a mobilehome park, in the City of San Diego. housing where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with the owner who lives there; single-family owner-occupied homes (including mobile homes) where the owner rents no more than 2 units or bedrooms (including ADU/JADU); duplexes where the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence at the start of the tenancy, if neither unit is an ADU/JADU; separately alienable units (e.g., condos) whose landlord is not a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with a corporate member, or a mobilehome park management and where the tenant received written notice of the exemption;
